messages:
maria: Heads-up — I repro'd the tenant fairness issue in staging. Short requests p99 blows up when mixed with long sequences. attaching quick summary and flamegraphs.
perf-bot: flamegraph: https://artifacts.internal/reports/2080011223/flame.svg
jake: can you paste the concise numbers?
maria: short requests (<64 tokens) p95 went from 48ms -> 72ms and p99 from 48ms -> 220ms in mixed workload. KV cache hit rate for short lanes drops ~12% during bursts. cpu profiles show long sequences holding batch slots longer due to kernel init+warm paths.
kevin: which kernel selector change correlates with this? commit?
maria: looks correlated with kernel-selector change def456 that prefers unified-kernel for long seqs — the init overhead stalls the batcher queue for ~10-30ms per long seq on cold paths.
sarah: did we try changing batch formation/window?
maria: ran two quick probes in staging:

1) "mini-slab" reservation: reserve N token-budget slots (N=8) exclusively for short requests (<64 tokens) per-worker. If unused, they spill to general pool. This prevents short requests from being preempted by in-flight long KERNEL_INIT work.
2) KV prewarm per-tenant: detect long request start and prewarm KV entries for likely short-follower requests (heuristic: same tenant + recent prefix similarity).

Results:
- mini-slab: short p99 reduced from 220ms -> 68ms (3.2x). throughput impact ~-2%.
- kv-prewarm: improves average latency for mixed traffic but only when memory budget available; under high long load the prewarm memory churn causes small GC spikes.

Also: after kernel-selector commit ghi789 (small followup), short-path fallback accidentally added a 12% CPU loop on hot path — that created a perf regression for micro-batches.
jake: mini-slab seems promising. Any telemetry we should add for canary?
maria: propose metrics: batch_slot_hold_ms (histogram), reserved_slab_utilization, kv_warm_ratio, per_tenant_queue_age_histogram. Also add a fast-kernel-availability gauge so scheduler can decide to avoid long-kernel init during slot allocation.
kevin: +1. Also capture per-tenant short-request-starve_count (counter) to detect if slab is starving other tenants.
sarah: what's the rollout plan?
jake: canary: 10% traffic on dedicated pool with slab+kv-prewarm, collect metrics for 30m windows. Fail conditions: short p99 > 150ms for >5m, reserved_slab_utilization consistently <10% (means wasted), or memory pressure + swap > 0.
maria: I'll open PR with the slab scheduler (sandbox POC at infra/perf/sandbox) and a test harness. Quick run command:

```
./bench mix --tenants 50 --mix short:60,long:40 --duration 15m --enable-mini-slab --slab-size 8
```

perf-bot: canary run summary (10% traffic, 50 tenants, 15m): short p99 from 220ms -> 68ms, overall throughput -2%, per-worker memory +200MB with kv-prewarm enabled, no CPU errors, batch_slot_hold_ms median down 18%.
kevin: memory +200MB needs review; may be ok in dedicated but not on smaller nodes.
sarah: ok start 10% canary. Roll to 25% if slab_utilization > 30% and short p99 < 100ms for two consecutive 30m windows. Add auto-fallback: if short p99 > 150ms for >5m rollback slab on that pool.
maria: noted. I'll add the telemetry tags and open the PR. Also will add a small microbenchmark to isolate the kernel-init regression (candidate revert def456 if we can't get fast-path).
jake: thanks — ping here when PR+canary URL ready.
kevin: thx
maria: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/2345 (WIP) — will update with perf artifacts after CI.
perf-bot: benchmark artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/reports/2080011223/
